title: Long-held visions of New York and Paris
summary: Waters compares his dream of New York with his dream of Paris, which he reached via Jimmy Archey's European trip and Bill Coleman, before leaving for ten years at La Cigalle.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: see. But I was, my vision, I say - suppose I put it this way, Phil, it won't be so technical. My vision from the very beginning, it's when I got so that I could play, I thought I was playin' quite well - it was New York, like everybody's vision, how I got there didn't matter. [ ] -
So you were willing to go the route -

My vision, I mean New York City is a big thing, you know what I'm saying, you know what I mean, you know? Like the same thing with - look, with the same thing in Paris. When I left here, I didn't go to Paris with Jimmy Archey.
But my vision was Paris, you know?

From the very beginning at Jimmy Ryan's on 52nd Street, when Jimmy says 'We're going to Europe', my vision was Paris. Do you know when I got to Paris - Jimmy never did play Paris - I got to Paris with Bill Coleman, see what I'm talkin' about, that's clear, that's the same way. But I, when the big Paris opened, Paris was somethin' else, I wanted to go to Paris, you see? I said maybe I'll go to Paris, I wish that I could go to Par-, you und-, you follow what I mean now? I hope that I'll go to Paris. I didn't, 'cause Jimmy didn't say nothin' about Paris, he said Europe. I didn't know until way later he was even going to Hamburg. When we first landed on the airplane from New York, with the first place we landed was Hamburg. Well, I had Paris in my mind, see, that's why when I took Dicky Wells' place in Switzerland with Bill Coleman and I says, and Bill - I knew that Bill lived in Paris. So I said 'Ah, this is a chance for me to go', I still wasn't in Paris yet. Well, that kinda goes with what you're talkin', Atlantic City and New York and all that. I still wasn't in Paris, but that's my idea. And not only that, it proved that's my idea the first chance I got to leave Bill, I quit Bill

and went to Paris and worked for 10 years at Small's Paradise - I mean at the La Cigalle. See, so my idea was still, so now, see, I quit the band in Italy and went to Paris to just see Paris. Paris was somethin' big, just like New York was, at these lines. Understand? (laughs). Long as you're working -
